questions.question: What is the expected major product when Potassium phthalimide is treated with 1. 1-Bromopentane in DMF; 2. Hydrazine (N2H4)?
questions.explanation: Treating Potassium phthalimide with 1. 1-Bromopentane in DMF; 2. Hydrazine (N2H4) yields 1-Pentanamine + Phthalhydrazide. Rationale: Phthalimide anion alkylation via SN2 followed by hydrazinolysis yields pure primary alkylamine.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Benzaldehyde + Methylamine into N-Methylbenzylamine?
questions.explanation: To convert Benzaldehyde + Methylamine into N-Methylbenzylamine, the appropriate reagent is Sodium cyanoborohydride (NaBH3CN). Rationale: Carbonyl and primary amine condense to imine, which is selectively reduced by mild NaBH3CN.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when 2-Butanamine is treated with 1. Excess CH3I; 2. Ag2O, H2O; 3. Heat?
questions.explanation: Treating 2-Butanamine with 1. Excess CH3I; 2. Ag2O, H2O; 3. Heat yields 1-Butene (major) + Trimethylamine + H2O. Rationale: Exhaustive methylation forms quaternary ammonium; bulky leaving group eliminates toward less hindered alkene.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) into Aniline (PhNH2) + CO2 + N2?
questions.explanation: To convert Benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) into Aniline (PhNH2) + CO2 + N2, the appropriate reagent is 1. NaN3; 2. Heat; 3. H2O. Rationale: Acyl azide intermediate undergoes thermal rearrangement to isocyanate (PhN=C=O), hydrolyzed to primary amine.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Aniline (PhNH2) is treated with Sodium nitrite (NaNO2) / aqueous HCl (0-5°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating Aniline (PhNH2) with Sodium nitrite (NaNO2) / aqueous HCl (0-5°C) yields Benzenediazonium chloride (PhN2+ Cl-). Rationale: Nitrous acid (HONO) reacts with primary aromatic amine at low temperature to generate stable diazonium salt.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Benzenediazonium chloride into Chlorobenzene + N2 gas?
questions.explanation: To convert Benzenediazonium chloride into Chlorobenzene + N2 gas, the appropriate reagent is Copper(I) chloride (CuCl). Rationale: Copper(I) catalyzed replacement of diazonium group with chlorine on the aromatic ring.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Copper(I) cyanide (CuCN) to yield Benzonitrile (PhCN) + N2 gas as the major product?
questions.explanation: Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with Copper(I) cyanide (CuCN) to yield Benzonitrile (PhCN) + N2 gas. Rationale: Copper(I) catalyzed substitution replaces the diazonium group with a cyano group.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Benzenediazonium chloride is treated with 1. HBF4; 2. Heat?
questions.explanation: Treating Benzenediazonium chloride with 1. HBF4; 2. Heat yields Fluorobenzene + BF3 + N2 gas. Rationale: Thermal decomposition of aryl diazonium tetrafluoroborate yields fluorobenzene cleanly.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Hypophosphorous acid (H3PO2) in H2O to yield Benzene + N2 gas + H3PO3 + HCl as the major product?
questions.explanation: Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with Hypophosphorous acid (H3PO2) in H2O to yield Benzene + N2 gas + H3PO3 + HCl. Rationale: Hypophosphorous acid acts as a hydride donor to reduce the diazonium group to a C-H bond.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Benzenediazonium chloride + Phenol is treated with Dilute aqueous NaOH (0°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating Benzenediazonium chloride + Phenol with Dilute aqueous NaOH (0°C) yields 4-(Phenyldiazenyl)phenol (p-hydroxyazobenzene, orange dye). Rationale: Electrophilic aromatic substitution of diazonium cation para to phenol hydroxyl forms an extended azo chromophore.
